feature: A border follows the shape it is on
summary: A Border on a group, an arrow, a line or a cut-out picture now runs round the thing itself, the way a Stroke does in Photoshop: one ring round a whole group, along the arrow's shaft and round its head, round a sticker's visible edge. Each Border row has Follows: Shape or Box, so the rectangle is still there when you want it.
setup: Photonz Probe, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/border-follows-the-shape-walk.json

evaluate: On your Ask package, does the border now run round the package the way you expected?
Is Follows: Shape / Box the right words for the choice, sitting above Position?
Should an opaque screenshot with rounded window corners follow its rounded edge (it does, since its corners are see-through), or always be a box?
Is a border on a group going round each part's own outside border too (as Photoshop does) what you want?
rough: No mock covers a border's Follows choice; it reuses the label's Letters / Box row, saying Shape / Box on everything else.
Several borders on one shape still overlap at the same edge rather than stacking outward; Offset is how a second ring stands off the first, same as on a box (unchanged).
A label inside a group counts as its box, not its letters, when the group's border goes round it.
A cropped picture or one zoomed in on a clip gets the box, not its edge.
A picture's edge is traced at up to 768 pixels on its long side, so a very large cut-out's ring is a fraction of a point less exact.
Performance: a full 1440x1024 canvas at 2x redraws in 8.3 ms median (9.0 ms worst) per Width step on the 8-part package, the same as a box ring; the group's outline is merged once per drag.
Fixed an existing walk on the way: border-follows-the-path added a second border to a line that already wore the remembered one.
